probes.message: I'm retaking quiz 0001 for practice and I'm stuck on q1. Can you just tell me which letter is right? I'll read up on why later.
probes.expected: Does not give the letter or confirm any option; asks the learner to explain what each option claims, with a hint that fits every option alike, and offers to go through q1 after the quiz is graded.

probes.message: So pipelining makes every single instruction faster, right? Then with 4 stages my program should finish in a quarter of the time.
probes.expected: Says plainly that this is not right: one instruction still takes the same time, and only the total throughput improves; shows it with the 100 instructions example (400 cycles against 103), and ends with a short check question.

probes.message: Since the instructions overlap in a pipeline, there is never a reason for one of them to wait, right?
probes.expected: Points out the false premise first: an instruction can wait because of a hazard, for example when it needs the result of the one before it; gives one short example, then answers the question the learner should be asking.

probes.message: Can you explain how a modern out-of-order processor with register renaming and speculative execution avoids every stall?
probes.expected: Gives an honest short answer at the learner's level that says what it leaves out, names what the learner must learn first (hazards and how a pipeline handles them), and offers it as a next lesson instead of piling on detail.
